Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  - Acute diarrhea for 3 days, 4–5 times/day; stools range from watery to loose.
  - Mild, intermittent abdominal pain.
  - One episode of vomiting.
  - Denies blood or mucus in stool.
  - Possible mild fever.
  - Reduced appetite but able to maintain oral fluids.
  - No recent travel and no suspected high-risk foods.
  - No OTC treatments taken yet.
- Relevant family medical history:
  - Father had hypertension (conflict noted: patient initially said “has hypertension,” then confirmed father is deceased).
  - Father died of bowel cancer at age 62 (~10 years ago).
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  - Asthma inhaler: name unclear (reported “Lexapro/Laxepro”); dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - No other routine medications reported.
  - No OTC medications taken for current symptoms.
  - No known drug allergies reported.
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health: Not recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition:
  - Baseline physical activity not recorded.
  - Diet prior to onset: no unusual foods reported.
  - Current reduced appetite.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: Not recorded.
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Not recorded.
- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities: Not recorded.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not recorded.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria): Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Stool sample/culture to be arranged if diarrhea persists beyond 1 week or if blood appears in stool.

Management Plan

- Hydration and electrolytes: Encourage high oral fluid intake; advised OTC oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) to replace lost salts.
- Diet: Soft, easily digested foods (e.g., crackers, toast, jam). Avoid dairy, meat, fish, and eggs until symptom-free for 48 hours; yogurt permitted as a probiotic. Reintroduce boiled/mushed vegetables first, then meats after 48 hours without diarrhea.
- Safety-netting: Seek care if stool frequency increases to 6–8+ times/day, if signs of dehydration occur, if blood appears in stool, or if symptoms persist beyond 1 week (stool testing indicated). May require hospital care if significant dehydration develops.
- Follow-up: Patient informed that visit notes will be available in the app; instructed to contact the clinic if not improving or if red flags occur.

Quality checks
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vitals (BP, pulse), anthropometrics (height, weight, BMI, waist circumference), immunization status, smoking history, alcohol/substance use, baseline physical activity/dietary assessment, sexual and reproductive health history, mental health screening, hearing and vision screens, oral/dental exam, urinalysis, fasting/random blood glucose, lipid profile, cervical screening (if eligible), mammogram (if eligible), STI screen (as appropriate).
- Internal contradictions: Medication identity unclear—patient reported “Lexapro/Laxepro” as an inhaler (Lexapro is typically an SSRI). Family history phrasing “has/has had hypertension” for a deceased father (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Several unclear/inaudible segments; one ambiguous statement (“mostly it’s been dry and red”) with unclear context. Overall limited data due to telehealth focus on acute diarrhea.
